faults.finding: "For the same power a lower voltage needs more current" is asserted, not shown. The step that makes it obvious is the rule already taught: the power is √3 × voltage × current × power factor, so with the power fixed, a smaller voltage leaves a larger current.
faults.fix: Add that step in one clause in explain; the written point already carries the rule.

faults.finding: "With neither given, work with both as 1" is wrong for a motor: a motor has an efficiency and a power factor whether or not someone has handed them over, and without the nameplate or maker's data its true Ib cannot be found. Only a load with nothing to allow for (the slides' heater) is worked at 1 and 1.
faults.fix: Say a heater like the slides' is worked at 1 and 1, and a motor's figures come from its nameplate or the maker's data (slides p.14 on the card).

faults.fault: interactive brief shows only the effect
faults.finding: The brief names Ib climbing but not the cause the bars draw: the input bar stretching past the output, then the apparent bar past the input.
faults.fix: Name the two bars stretching as the cause of the climb.

faults.fault: wrong why in a slip's feedback
faults.finding: "Three-phase power is shared by three lines, so the rule divides by √3 × the line voltage" invites dividing by 3, not √3; it does not explain the √3.
faults.fix: Say what 50.00 A treats the heater as (one line at 400 V carrying all of it) and give the rule, P = √3 × UL × IL × pf (slides p.13), without a false reason.

faults.finding: The recall heater's 20 kW is the slides' own example (p.16), not an assumed value; the 90 °C cable is a given from the pack with no research quote.
faults.fix: Make 20 kW a constant cited to [32]; label 90 °C as the pack's given.

faults.finding: The three bars share one scale, but the draft does not say what the scale must fit; at 0.70 and 0.70 the apparent bar is 40.81 kVA, twice the output, and could run off a 340 px frame.
faults.fix: Say the scale fits the largest bar, 40.81 kVA, at the lowest settings.

faults.finding: "The extra current ... flows back and forth": it is the reactive power that surges between supply and the motor's magnetic field each cycle; the current that carries it is what heats the cable.

checked_and_sound: No recall-only checks: read mode, checks [] (the screen 4 check applies the rule with named slips).
Research is not decorative: each point carries a quote from his slides or a researched page; the delta relation now has its quote ([16]).
The explanation teaches the idea (output to input to apparent power to current) rather than describing it.

Refresher pattern: recall with Refresh the why / Skip to the practice (skip only on a right answer, landing on screen 7); what it is for; the why with its interactive; a check; the worked example with the slides' cut-short figures noted; Section A 1(a) and 1(b) with the scenario, carried part and typed answers; Section B with K.written b1; one changed-numbers item; Keep this with the summary. Eleven screens. No timers, marks or grades.
